summary: No reconnect/resync logic: a WebTransport drop mid-game wedges the phone permanently with no way to recover, taking the player out of the game.
scenario: Phone loses QUIC session mid-round (congested venue Wi-Fi / IP migration). client.ts handleClose fires onState(false) -> conn becomes 'disconnected'. But clientRef.current is still the dead client, view.joined stays true, and NOTHING attempts to reconnect. The user is stuck on a dead buzzer screen; they cannot even rejoin because connect() early-returns on the stale clientRef, and JoinScreen is never re-shown (joined=true). The server's sendFullSync/resync path (mobile-safe, sanitized) is never invoked because no new session or resync frame is ever sent. Player is silently eliminated for the rest of the game.
suggested_fix: On onState(false): if not intentionally closed, clear clientRef, and either auto-reconnect (new GameClient -> connect -> re-send hello with the SAME getDeviceFP() + saved handle -> send {t:'resync'}) with backoff, or at minimum flip joined=false so JoinScreen re-appears and the player can rejoin. A dropped mid-game connection must resync to sanitized state, not wedge.

summary: Heartbeat interval is only cleared on component unmount, not on disconnect; after a drop it keeps calling send() on a dead writer every 2s, producing a steady stream of unhandled promise rejections.
scenario: Connection drops but the App component stays mounted (which it does — see uimobile-1). clientRef.current is still non-null, so sendHeartbeat keeps firing every 2s. client.send() calls writer.write() on a closed/errored stream, whose rejected promise is swallowed by `void`, generating an unhandled rejection every 2 seconds indefinitely and needlessly stamping pendingPing. This runs forever on a wedged buzzer.
suggested_fix: Stop the heartbeat when onState(false) fires (clearInterval(heartbeatRef.current); heartbeatRef.current=null), and restart it only on a successful (re)connect. Also await/catch c.send in sendHeartbeat so a failed write is handled rather than left as an unhandled rejection.

summary: Status label shows 'reconnecting' on the disconnected state even though the client never attempts to reconnect — the UI lies about recovery being in progress.
scenario: After a WT drop, conn='disconnected' and the pulsing red dot reads 'reconnecting' forever, so the player waits indefinitely for a recovery that will never happen instead of manually reloading the PWA. Misleading UX that hides the wedge.
suggested_fix: Either implement real reconnect (uimobile-1) so the label is truthful, or label it 'disconnected — reload to rejoin' and surface a reload/rejoin action.

summary: DeviceFP (player identity) is a plain random UUID in localStorage; clearing site data resets identity, so a ban is trivially evadable (and a legit player who clears storage loses their score). By design, but worth flagging.
scenario: A banned attendee opens the buzzer in an incognito tab or clears site data -> getDeviceFP mints a fresh UUID -> re-sends hello with a new deviceFP -> server sees a brand-new player and the ban (keyed on DeviceFP) is bypassed. Conversely a normal user who clears storage silently forfeits their accumulated score. The zero-trust model already assumes a hostile client, so this is an inherent limitation, not a client exploit per se — but bans must not rely on this value alone.
suggested_fix: Accept as a documented limitation on the client side; enforce bans server-side on a signal the client cannot cheaply reset (IP/subnet + connection-level heuristics, which the engine already tracks via cheatReport) rather than trusting DeviceFP as a durable identity.

summary: awaitingBuzzResult is set true on buzz but never reset on disconnect or round transition; a stale buzzResult{won:false} arriving later can spuriously mark the player buzzed-and-lost.
scenario: Player taps GUESS but the buzz frame's result is delayed/dropped (or the round resets before the buzzResult arrives). awaitingBuzzResult stays true across the round boundary. A later buzzResult{won:false} (e.g. a late frame, or the next round) flips buzzedAndLost=true, locking the player's buzzer out of a round they never buzzed in.
suggested_fix: Reset awaitingBuzzResult.current=false in the 'state' handler whenever a fresh ROUND_ACTIVE begins (same place buzzedAndLost is reset) and on disconnect, so only a result for the current in-flight buzz can set buzzedAndLost.

summary: pendingPing is never cleared on disconnect; a heartbeat echo received after a reconnect can be matched against a pre-disconnect send timestamp, yielding a wildly inflated RTT reading.
scenario: A heartbeat is sent (pendingPing stamped), the connection stalls for several seconds, then recovers. The next heartbeat echo subtracts the old timestamp and reports an RTT of thousands of ms, which also feeds lastRtt back to the server in the heartbeat payload. Cosmetic on the phone but pollutes the RTT signal the server/telemetry rely on.
suggested_fix: Clear pendingPing.current=null on onState(false), and ignore/clamp echoes whose elapsed time exceeds a sane bound (e.g. > a few heartbeat intervals).
